metadata.title: Week 7 KP06 ResNet, residual learning
metadata.description: IDL 2026 Week 7 KP06; reasoning-led-teaching-deck 2.2.0; English, self-paced reading; manual advance, try before reveal

p01-degradation-title.name: p01-degradation-title
p01-degradation-title.text: Both are called 'getting worse' — how do overfitting and degradation differ?

p01-degradation-ctx.name: p01-degradation-ctx
p01-degradation-ctx.text: Beyond about $20$ layers, making the network deeper makes results worse. First see which metric gets worse (bar heights are a sketch, not measured).

p01-degradation-ta.name: p01-degradation-ta
p01-degradation-ta.text: Overfitting: two metrics of the same network

p01-degradation-dropt.name: p01-degradation-dropt
p01-degradation-dropt.text:
Even the 'training' accuracy falls
⇒ an optimization problem (degradation),
not memorizing too much

p02-identity-title.name: p02-identity-title
p02-identity-title.text: Why should a deeper network, in theory, be no worse than a shallow one?

p02-identity-ctx.name: p02-identity-ctx
p02-identity-ctx.text: Imagine attaching a few extra layers after a shallow network, and those layers change nothing (output equals input).

p02-identity-out.name: p02-identity-out
p02-identity-out.text:
Deep network output
= shallow network output

p02-identity-hurdle.name: p02-identity-hurdle
p02-identity-hurdle.text:
But plain layers must 'find' $W=I$:
all weights must equal the identity matrix exactly —
hard to optimize

p02-identity-res.name: p02-identity-res
p02-identity-res.text:
⇒ In theory a deep network should not be worse,
yet in practice it is:
plain layers cannot learn the identity

p03-residual-title.name: p03-residual-title
p03-residual-title.text: How to make this group of layers easily become the identity? Learn only the 'difference'

p03-residual-ctx.name: p03-residual-ctx
p03-residual-ctx.text: The usual way: a group of layers learns the target mapping $\mathcal{H}(x)$ directly. ResNet instead lets it learn the difference between target and input.

p03-residual-e2.name: p03-residual-e2
p03-residual-e2.text:
Main path learns $\mathcal{F}=0$:
$\mathcal{H}=0+x=x$ — output equals input (identity)

p03-residual-sp.name: p03-residual-sp
p03-residual-sp.text: If shapes differ (e.g. channel count changes), put a $1\times1$ conv on the shortcut first [supplement]

p04-easy-identity-title.name: p04-easy-identity-title
p04-easy-identity-title.text: Reason 1: how far from the initial value is the weight that identity needs?

p04-easy-identity-ctx.name: p04-easy-identity-ctx
p04-easy-identity-ctx.text: A minimal sketch with one weight $w$ ([supplement]): plain layer $y=wx$, residual block $y=wx+x$. Initial weights are usually small random numbers (KP01), near $0$.

p04-easy-identity-tpt.name: p04-easy-identity-tpt
p04-easy-identity-tpt.text:
Plain layer: identity needs $w=1$
distance from initial ≈ $1$ (a long way to learn)

p04-easy-identity-trt.name: p04-easy-identity-trt
p04-easy-identity-trt.text:
Residual block: identity needs $w=0$
distance from initial ≈ $0$ (already nearby)

p05-gradient-title.name: p05-gradient-title
p05-gradient-title.text: Reason 2: through twenty layers multiplied together, how much gradient is left?

p05-gradient-ctx.name: p05-gradient-ctx
p05-gradient-ctx.text: The chain rule multiplies each layer's derivative. If each block's derivative is $1$ plus a small number, the product does not collapse easily (derivatives are assumed values, not measured).

p05-gradient-dv.name: p05-gradient-dv
p05-gradient-dv.text: $\dfrac{\partial\mathcal H}{\partial x}=\dfrac{\partial\mathcal F}{\partial x}+1$　($+1$ comes from the shortcut)

p05-gradient-zt.name: p05-gradient-zt
p05-gradient-zt.text: Nearly-vanished gradient zone (an illustrative split, not a threshold from the lecture)

p06-practice-a-title.name: p06-practice-a-title
p06-practice-a-title.text: Your turn: what does this residual block output? What should the main path learn for identity?

p06-practice-a-ctx.name: p06-practice-a-ctx
p06-practice-a-ctx.text: Answer from the figure first, then press Next for feedback. The numbers are new ($x=2$, main-path output $-0.5$).

p06-practice-a-q2.name: p06-practice-a-q2
p06-practice-a-q2.text: Q2: for the output to equal the input, what should the main path $\mathcal{F}$ be?

p07-free-title.name: p07-free-title
p07-free-title.text: How many extra weights does the shortcut cost?

p07-free-ctx.name: p07-free-ctx
p07-free-ctx.text: Take a residual block with $C=64$ channels: two $3\times3$ conv layers on the main path.

p07-free-eq.name: p07-free-eq
p07-free-eq.text: Also $73{,}728$: the shortcut adds no weights

p08-variants-title.name: p08-variants-title
p08-variants-title.text: ResNet-18, 34, 50, 101: what do the numbers mean, and how to use them?

p08-variants-ctx.name: p08-variants-ctx
p08-variants-ctx.text: The number is the network's layer count.

p08-variants-l18.name: p08-variants-l18
p08-variants-l18.text: Laptop-scale tasks: ResNet-18 is often enough

p08-variants-bnote.name: p08-variants-bnote
p08-variants-bnote.text: The 'bottleneck block' of the deeper 50- and 101-layer versions: reduce, then restore — the same idea as the dimension reduction in KP04 [supplement]

p08-variants-bk2.name: p08-variants-bk2
p08-variants-bk2.text: Put research effort elsewhere (e.g. a new loss function)

p09-stack-title.name: p09-stack-title
p09-stack-title.text: Optional: ten 'add a little' blocks — by what factor does the output grow?

p09-stack-ctx.name: p09-stack-ctx
p09-stack-ctx.text: [Supplement] Each block has $\mathcal{F}(x)=0.1\,x$, so each block gives $\mathcal{H}=0.1x+x=1.1\,x$.

p09-stack-warn.name: p09-stack-warn
p09-stack-warn.text:
The output keeps growing: a residual block 'adds a little' to the input; it does not 'leave it unchanged'.
Stacking many needs normalization and a suitable initialization (KP01).

p10-practice-b-title.name: p10-practice-b-title
p10-practice-b-title.text: Your turn: ten blocks multiplied, weights for C=128, why it is not overfitting

p10-practice-b-ctx.name: p10-practice-b-ctx
p10-practice-b-ctx.text: Answer first, then advance for feedback.

p10-practice-b-q1.name: p10-practice-b-q1
p10-practice-b-q1.text: Q1: stack ten blocks with $\mathcal{F}(x)=0.1\,x$ — the output is how many times the input?

p10-practice-b-q2.name: p10-practice-b-q2
p10-practice-b-q2.text: Q2: how many weights in the two-layer main path? How many in the identity shortcut?

p10-practice-b-q3.name: p10-practice-b-q3
p10-practice-b-q3.text: Q3: training accuracy falls with depth — why is that not overfitting?

p10-practice-b-a3.name: p10-practice-b-a3
p10-practice-b-a3.text: Overfitting means training good, test bad; here even training itself falls → the problem is optimization, not memorizing too much

p11-misconceptions-title.name: p11-misconceptions-title
p11-misconceptions-title.text: Which of these four statements is wrong, and where?

p11-misconceptions-ctx.name: p11-misconceptions-ctx
p11-misconceptions-ctx.text: Judge each one yourself first, then see the correction.

p11-misconceptions-c0.name: p11-misconceptions-c0
p11-misconceptions-c0.text: Plain networks beyond about $20$ layers get worse training accuracy.

p11-misconceptions-c1.name: p11-misconceptions-c1
p11-misconceptions-c1.text: Overfitting is training good, test bad.

p11-misconceptions-m2.name: p11-misconceptions-m2
p11-misconceptions-m2.text: 'The shortcut makes the later layers useless.'

p11-misconceptions-c2.name: p11-misconceptions-c2
p11-misconceptions-c2.text: The main path's $\mathcal{F}$ still learns; the output is the sum of both.

p11-misconceptions-c3.name: p11-misconceptions-c3
p11-misconceptions-c3.text: An identity shortcut has no weights, just one extra addition.

p12-quiz-ctx.name: p12-quiz-ctx
p12-quiz-ctx.text: From the source's four questions, the first two; the source gives no answers, so the answers and explanations are written for this lecture ([supplement]).

p12-quiz-q0.name: p12-quiz-q0
p12-quiz-q0.text:
What does the 'degradation problem' mean?
A. Beyond 3 layers a network can never be trained
B. Beyond about 20 layers, going deeper can make training accuracy saturate or even fall
C. Pooling makes all gradients zero
D. Only U-Net suffers from it, classification networks do not

p12-quiz-a0.name: p12-quiz-a0
p12-quiz-a0.text: Answer B. After about 20 layers training accuracy first saturates and then falls; A turns the layer count into 3, and C, D have nothing to do with degradation.

p12-quiz-q1.name: p12-quiz-q1
p12-quiz-q1.text:
What do the residual-learning formulas (9)(10) mean?
A. Directly require $\mathcal{H}(x)=0$
B. The layers learn $\mathcal{F}(x):=\mathcal{H}(x)-x$, and the target mapping is written $\mathcal{H}(x)=\mathcal{F}(x)+x$
C. Replace all convolutions with fully connected layers
D. Forbid ReLU

p12-quiz-a1.name: p12-quiz-a1
p12-quiz-a1.text: Answer B. The layers learn the residual F and the output adds x back; A, C, D are not residual learning.

p13-summary-title.name: p13-summary-title
p13-summary-title.text: The whole KP06 reasoning chain at a glance

p13-summary-ctx.name: p13-summary-ctx
p13-summary-ctx.text: Every arrow is a conclusion from an earlier page.

p13-summary-ch1.name: p13-summary-ch1
p13-summary-ch1.text:
Extra layers should learn identity,
but plain layers cannot find $W=I$

p13-summary-ch2.name: p13-summary-ch2
p13-summary-ch2.text:
Learn the residual instead
$\mathcal H=\mathcal F+x$

p13-summary-ch3.name: p13-summary-ch3
p13-summary-ch3.text:
Identity = weights $\to0$ (near initial)
gradient = small number + $1$

p13-summary-ch4.name: p13-summary-ch4
p13-summary-ch4.text:
Shortcut: $0$ weights
⇒ can stack very deep, serve as backbone

p13-summary-next.name: p13-summary-next
p13-summary-next.text:
Question for the next unit: instead of 'adding', what if the outputs of 'all earlier layers' are connected in?
⇒ KP07 DenseNet (also EfficientNet, ConvNeXt, and a review of the whole chapter)
